page_title: Catalog of Patterns of Distributed Systems

summary.title: Catalog of Patterns of Distributed Systems
summary.one_liner: A catalog of reusable design patterns, from clocks and leader election to logs and consensus, for building and explaining distributed systems.
keywords: how do distributed systems order events
how to handle leader election without an election
takeaways: Distributed systems commonly rely on a set of recurring solutions such as leader-follower replication, quorums, and write-ahead logs.
Clock patterns (Lamport clock, hybrid clock, clock-bound wait) show how to order values across nodes with uncertain time.
Leases, heartbeats, generation clocks, and emergent leaders help nodes coordinate and detect failures without explicit elections.
Partitioning and log patterns (fixed partitions, key-range partitions, segmented log, high-water mark) address scaling and durability.
Each pattern has a one-line summary here, with deeper chapters in the book Patterns of Distributed Systems (2023).
summary.summary: This page is an index of patterns for designing distributed systems, written by Martin Fowler's site and later published as a book in 2023. Each pattern gets a one-to-two sentence summary covering topics such as time and ordering, cluster coordination, replication, partitioning, networking, and durability. Entries link to chapters of the online eBook for fuller explanations. The page itself is a short catalog, so it works best as a quick reference or a map to the detailed material.
